subject.title: [Bug]: Discord sessions persist per-session exec directives, causing allowlist mode to behave unexpectedly after config changes

question: Should stored `/exec` host/security/ask/node session overrides continue to outrank current global or per-agent exec config after restart, or should operator config changes invalidate or override them?
rationale: The current behavior is documented and tested as durable session state, but it is also security-sensitive because older sessions can preserve weaker exec policy after an operator tightens config.

options.title: Add explicit invalidation or reset semantics
options.body: Keep `/exec` as a session default, but clear or invalidate stored exec overrides when the relevant exec policy changes, or expose an operator reset/doctor path with tests and docs.

options.title: Preserve current durable `/exec` precedence
options.body: Treat the current documented session-state behavior as intentional and close this after adding clearer operator guidance about resetting old sessions.

options.title: Make current config always win
options.body: Change precedence so global/per-agent exec config overrides stored session exec fields, accepting the compatibility impact for users relying on per-session defaults.

recommendation.title: Add explicit invalidation or reset semantics
recommendation.body: Keep `/exec` as a session default, but clear or invalidate stored exec overrides when the relevant exec policy changes, or expose an operator reset/doctor path with tests and docs.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest feature-history signal for `/exec` session override semantics and its current tests points to steipete-authored commits.
